cases.name: minimal
cases.why: one log, one witness, one quorum

cases.name: no-trailing-newline
cases.why: the final line's newline is optional

cases.name: blank-and-whitespace-lines
cases.why: a line that is empty, or only spaces and tabs, is ignored

cases.name: nested-group
cases.why: a group may name a group; it counts as one member, satisfied or not

cases.name: no-log-line
cases.why: `log` is not required by the grammar: the trust file carries the log key

cases.name: comment-and-indent
cases.why: a line whose first non-space character is `#` is ignored, and leading spaces and tabs are not part of a field

cases.name: bad-vertical-tab
cases.why: only ASCII space and tab separate fields, anywhere in a line

cases.name: bad-forward-reference
cases.why: a group names previously-defined members only

cases.name: bad-two-quorums
cases.why: there is exactly one quorum line

cases.name: bad-no-quorum
cases.why: there is exactly one quorum line

cases.name: bad-empty-group
cases.why: a group has at least one member

cases.name: bad-unknown-keyword
cases.why: every line is one of the four directives

cases.name: bad-quorum-undefined
cases.why: the quorum names something the policy defines

comment: SPEC 9.1's restated `tlog-policy` grammar, one whole policy per rule, each differing from a valid one in exactly one way. A case with `accept` true MUST parse; the rest MUST be refused. The text is the file verbatim -- some cases turn on whether it ends in a newline
